acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Giants family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Hill Giant, T2, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Slope-Roll Pressure Soldier (Soldier) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two normal construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Four times human height, with moss on the shoulders, first stone plates along the back, a thick rope belt, and several boulders carried in oversized rope cradles.

Signature mechanic: Hill Roll: the Giant unhooks one boulder from its rope belt, braces it against a forming back plate, and releases it along the lower of two visible slopes; the empty rope loop then drags behind and can be stepped on during retrieval.
battlefieldDuty: Apply repeatable ranged pressure by hauling and releasing rope-cradled boulders down selected lanes, then occupying the new low ground behind them.
constructionDimensions: Anatomy and materials stay naturally weathered: thick skin, rough hide, ordinary raw stone plates, moss, lichen, pines, rope, and iron chain accumulate through age and scale rather than magical replacement.
Motion and wake remain physical and local: muscle loading, chain drag, loose scree, falling needles, water runoff, and impact dust reveal mass without persistent elemental trails or luminous anatomy.
counterplay: Move to higher ground or behind the dropped tree cover, then pin or cut the empty dragging loop before the Giant retrieves another boulder. Affinity signal: Hands, heels, rope knots, chain pivots, rune anchors, unstable shelves, and ordinary fracture seams remain visible at every scale as the form's established weak points.
forbiddenTreatments: Landscape coverage that obscures the Giant's humanoid joints and committed weight shifts
identityInvariants: Humanlike proportions scaled upward with a heavy brow, thick limbs, dense bone, and a slight stoop that communicates the body's own weight.
Stone grey, granite blue-grey, earth brown, moss green, glacier white, and warm amber eyes remain the family palette without requiring an elemental origin.
Rough hide, raw stone, moss, lichen, pine, iron chain, and rope accumulate as bodily geology and oversized practical tools.
Chains, standing-stone jewelry, skin runes, and whole trees function as ornament at a scale that stays legible from the arena.
Raw scale and geological coverage escalate together until the Sovereign carries a valley, but every form retains recognizable humanoid load paths and slow committed motion.
telegraph: Moss sheds from one shoulder, the corresponding rope loop pulls taut, and the Giant tests the ground with a broad foot before turning the boulder downhill.
